r5900-mfc1.status: qualified per source for USA level bodies only
r5900-mfc1.provenance: GNU EE assembler built from OpenRAC/rac2-decomp's versioned R5900 mfc1 interlock source transformation (tools/compiler/transformers/r5900_mfc1_interlock.py, commit e07c4844d64b007377031e49c683d57fba8db07c). The patch exempts only mfc1 from the obsolete coprocessor-load delay while keeping the retail floating-condition delay. The separately measured 148-byte level body is exact at all 20 USA placements; the base assembler remains the route for all other accepted sources. A 436-byte level body that stores a float through its integer bits (mfc1 followed by a store) links with 31 differing words under the base assembler and exactly with this route at its twelve USA placements, from one representative and eleven per-placement address variants (November 2026). A 440-byte and a 104-byte level body whose retail code branches right after an mfc1 link 444 and 108 bytes (90 and 16 differing words) under the base assembler, which inserts a nop after the mfc1, and exactly with this route at fourteen USA placements, from two representatives and eleven per-placement address variants (November 2026). A 248-byte level body links 252 bytes (29 differing words) under the base assembler, which inserts a nop after an mfc1, and exactly with this route at its seventeen USA placements from one source (November 2026). A 684-byte level body links 692 bytes (76 differing words) under the base assembler for the same reason and exactly with this route at two USA placements, from one representative and one per-placement address variant (November 2026). A 780-byte level body links 784 bytes (24 differing words) under the base assembler, which inserts a nop after its final mfc1, and exactly with this route at sixteen USA placements, from one representative and fifteen per-placement address variants (November 2026). Two adjacent level bodies of 380 and 384 bytes link 384 and 388 bytes (26 and 29 differing words) under the base assembler for the same reason and exactly with this route at twenty USA placements each, from one representative and nineteen per-placement address variants of each (November 2026). A 460-byte level body links 468 bytes (92 differing words) under the base assembler for the same reason and exactly with this route at its USA placement (November 2026). A 556-byte and a 604-byte level body link 560 and 608 bytes (20 and 24 differing words) under the base assembler for the same reason and exactly with this route at twenty and two USA placements, from one representative and nineteen per-placement address variants and from one source (November 2026). Level bodies of 1,012, 664 and 304 bytes link 1,016, 668 and 308 bytes (15, 76 and 16 differing words) under the base assembler for the same reason and exactly with this route at sixteen, one and three USA placements, each from one representative and its per-placement address variants (November 2026). This external binary is hash-pinned and never committed; tools/compiler/build_gnu_ee.sh r5900-mfc1 rebuilds it from the public archive with patches/0000-rac5-pinned-base.patch and patches/0008-rac5-gas-r5900-mfc1.patch, which give that recipe's tc-mips.c (35a06b9a...). A 412-byte level body at LEVEL_15:0x0F7200 and LEVEL_21:0x0F7200 is exact only with this assembler: the base assembler adds the obsolete delay after one of its mfc1 instructions (416 bytes, 50 differing words from +0x30). A 420-byte level body links 424 bytes (11 differing words from +0x0C) under the base assembler, which adds the obsolete delay after an mfc1, and exactly with this route at three USA placements, from one representative and two per-placement address variants (November 2026). Level bodies of 416 and 524 bytes link 420 and 528 bytes (27 and 32 differing words) under the base assembler, which adds the obsolete delay after an mfc1, and exactly with this route at two USA placements each, from one representative and one per-placement address variant and from one source shared by two placements (November 2026). Fifteen address-variant copies of accepted bodies that are exact only with this route link exactly with it at their own pointer-only and nonzero-tail USA placements, like the accepted bodies they copy (November 2026).

ee-frozen.status: qualified per source for USA level bodies only
ee-frozen.provenance: Private EE assembler recovered with the legally supplied toolchain used in the RAC1 workspace. On the pinned USA body at LEVEL_01:0x001940, the default GNU assembler emits 96 bytes and misses the retail floating-point latency and delay-slot schedule; this hash-pinned binary emits the exact 100-byte body at all 20 numbered level placements. It is selected only for the measured source, never globally, and the external binary is not distributed. A per-placement address variant of LEVEL_02_08EA20.c is exact at its own USA placement with the same route (November 2026). The unpatched assembler of the public gnu-ee-binutils-gcc-1.1 archive (tools/compiler/build_gnu_ee.sh ee-frozen) assembles the three accepted sources of this route to the same objects as this binary (12 November 2026), so a gate run with --unpinned-tools can use it in its place.

ps2eeas.status: qualified per source for USA level bodies only
ps2eeas.provenance: SN Systems Ps2EeAs 1.8.19.316, the privately supplied EE assembler already pinned for the boot reconstruction in config/boot/compiler_trial.json. On the measured 192-byte level body the pinned GNU assembler expands the 64-bit constant as ori/dsll16 and links 216 bytes, while this assembler emits the retail lui/ori/dsll3/ori chain and reproduces all 18 USA placements exactly. A separate 132-byte body is exact at twenty USA placements from five per-source variants with the same pinned assembler. Two further 32- and 112-byte forms are exact at nineteen USA placements each; 36 new canonical source files use this same qualified per-source route, and the 21 complete modules remain exact. A 72-byte two-word record return links 72/72 bytes with one differing word under the pinned GNU assembler, which loads the 0xFFFFFFFF mask with lui instead of the retail addiu; this assembler reproduces all thirteen USA placements of that form from one source (November 2026). Five per-placement address variants of sources already on this route (LEVEL_02_0023B0.c, LEVEL_02_050448.c, LEVEL_02_06E1E0.c and LEVEL_03_0497A0.c) are exact at their own USA placements with the same route (November 2026). A 120-byte body links 120/120 bytes with one differing branch offset under the pinned GNU assembler, which places a floating-point hazard nop before a join label instead of after it; this assembler reproduces both of its USA placements from one source (November 2026). A 312-byte body links 320 bytes (57 differing words) under the pinned GNU assembler, which pads an aligned loop head with an extra nop, and exactly with this assembler at both of its USA placements from one source (November 2026). A 392-byte body links 392/392 bytes with one differing word under the pinned GNU assembler and exactly with this assembler at four USA placements, from one representative and three per-placement address variants (November 2026). A 432-byte body links 432/432 bytes with one differing word under the pinned GNU assembler, which places a nop before a label instead of after it, and exactly with this assembler at twenty USA placements, from one representative and nineteen per-placement address variants (November 2026). Selected only for the measured sources, never globally; the external binary is not distributed. A 680-byte body links 680/680 bytes with one differing word under the pinned GNU assembler, which puts an mtc1 hazard nop before a join label instead of after it, and exactly with this assembler at twenty-one USA placements, from one FRONTEND representative and twenty per-placement address variants (November 2026). A 456-byte body links 456/456 bytes with two differing words under the pinned GNU assembler, which expands the dli macro for the 64-bit constant 0x8000000000000000 as ori 0x8000; dsll32 16 where the retail code has addiu -1; dsll32 31, and exactly with this assembler at fifteen USA placements, from one representative and fourteen per-placement address variants (November 2026). A 568-byte body links 568/568 bytes with one differing word under the pinned GNU assembler, which expands the dli macro for the 64-bit mask 0xFFFFFFFF as lui 0xFFFF; dsrl32 where the retail code has addiu -1; dsrl32, and exactly with this assembler at one USA placement (November 2026).
